risk_if_not_implemented: Without Customized Development of Critical Components, applications may be built and deployed with exploitable design and coding weaknesses that adversaries can leverage. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), Third-Party Dependency Failure (R-SC-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) (TPM-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Customized Development of Critical Components (TDA-10) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a plan for Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance and disposal of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including documenting selected mitigating actions and monitoring performance against those plans.
compensating_control_2.justification: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan (RSK-20) provides risk identification and prioritization that compensates for the absence of Customized Development of Critical Components (TDA-10) by enabling informed decisions about where to focus resources to manage residual exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
